stem: Titanium is a transition element in Period 4. It is commonly found as $\text{TiO}_2$ in minerals.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Identify two typical properties of transition elements.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
The $\text{TiO}^{2+}$ ion forms when $\text{TiO}_2$ reacts with an excess of sulfuric acid.

$\text{TiO}^{2+}$ can be reduced by zinc metal in acidic conditions to form a purple solution containing $\text{Ti}^{3+}\text{(aq)}$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
$\text{TiO}^{2+}\text{(aq)}$ is a colourless ion.

Suggest why.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Give the electronic configuration of an isolated $\text{Ti}^{3+}$ ion.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Write an ionic equation for the reduction of $\text{TiO}^{2+}$ by zinc metal in acidic conditions.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem:
Acidified $\text{Ti}^{3+}\text{(aq)}$ reacts with oxygen dissolved in water as shown.

$$4\text{Ti}^{3+} + \text{O}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 4\text{TiO}^{2+} + 4\text{H}^+ \ \ \ \ \Delta G^\ominus = -436.1\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

The standard reduction potential, $E^\ominus$, of $\text{O}_2 + 4\text{H}^+ + 4\text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is $+1.23\text{ V}$.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the standard reduction potential, $E^\ominus$, in V, of the $\text{TiO}^{2+}\text{(aq)}/\text{Ti}^{3+}\text{(aq)}$ half-cell. Show your working.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
When aqueous citrate ions, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{O}_7^{3-}$, are added to $\text{Ti}^{3+}\text{(aq)}$, the $[\text{Ti}(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{O}_7)_2]^{3-}\text{(aq)}$ complex forms.

Explain, in terms of d-orbitals, why $\text{Ti}^{3+}$ is able to form complex ions.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
Acidified $[\text{Ti}(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{O}_7)_2]^{3-}\text{(aq)}$ does not react with oxygen dissolved in water, unlike acidified $\text{Ti}^{3+}\text{(aq)}$.

Suggest what this means for the value of the standard reduction potential, $E^\ominus$, of the following half-cell.

$$[\text{Ti}(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{O}_7)_2]^{2-}\text{(aq)} + \text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons [\text{Ti}(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{O}_7)_2]^{3-}\text{(aq)}$$

Explain your answer.

parts.stem:

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text:
The titanium ions in $\text{TiF}_6^{2-}$ and $\text{Ti(acac)}_2\text{Cl}_2$ have a coordination number of 6.

State what is meant by coordination number.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Write an equation for the formation of $\text{TiF}_6^{2-}$ from $\text{TiO}_2$.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text: State what is meant by bidentate ligand.

parts.label: (d)(iv)
parts.text:
$\text{Ti(acac)}_2\text{Cl}_2$ shows both optical and geometrical (cis/trans) isomerism.

$\text{Ti(acac)}_2\text{Cl}_2$ exists as three stereoisomers.

The structure of one stereoisomer of $\text{Ti(acac)}_2\text{Cl}_2$ is shown in Fig. 3.2.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}

Fig. 3.2

Complete the structures of the other two stereoisomers of $\text{Ti(acac)}_2\text{Cl}_2$.

{{figure:pdf_visual_03.png}}

parts.label: (d)(v)
parts.text:
The $\text{acac}^-$ anion is symmetrical.

Deduce which, if any, of stereoisomers 1, 2 and 3 in (d)(iv) are polar.

Explain your answer.
